title: Needles as skeleton of wave concentration
summary: Frequency cap of angular width δ on sphere ⇒ spatial tube width ~1/δ and length ~1/δ² (scaling as told). Union of multi-directional tubes is Kakeya-type; restriction becomes geometric tube packing.
math: Cap angular size δ ⇒ tube radius ∝ δ^{-1}, length ∝ δ^{-2} in the video's 3D scaling slogan.

title: Hollow needles: Furstenberg sets
summary: Relax Kakeya in two ways: (1) on each line keep only an s-dimensional dust (not full segment); (2) take only a t-dimensional family of lines (not every direction). Question: minimal Hausdorff dimension of the union.
math: Parameters s∈[0,1], t∈[0,2] in the plane (lines parameterized by 2 coords).

title: Ren–Wang 2023 planar theorem
summary: Every planar Furstenberg set has dim ≥ min(S+T, (3S+T)/2, S+1). Three regions of (S,T)-plane: additive regime, grid/middle, saturation. At S=T=1 recover dim≥2 = planar Kakeya (Davies) as special case. Sharp examples known; not mere lower bound culture.
math: dim ≥ min(s+t, (3s+t)/2, s+1). Boundaries t=s and t=2−s in the video map.

title: Two-ends and Restriction dictionary
summary: Two-ends inequality for line/tube bundles: mass cannot concentrate on a short segment of each line. Plane versions proved (full thickness later); 3D still conjectural. Conditional: two-ends ⇒ full restriction. Exponent↔dimension dictionary: e.g. popular 3.2 ↔ Kakeya 7/3; 22/7 ↔ Wolff 2.5. Solving 3D Kakeya does not automatically set restriction to 3.

title: Spillover applications
summary: Tools spill to Fefferman ball multiplier failure, Falconer distance, decoupling/Vinogradov mean value, local smoothing. Industrial slogan: not phone-app math—but each floor moves multiple pure-math fronts.
